summary: Mount Chase tower, Penobscot Co., ME: wooden tower 1909, steel tower 1917; moved in 2001 to the Patten Lumbermen's Museum, where it stands as a display.

facts.design: Steel tower erected 1917, listed as 16 ft (1920 inventory says 12 ft); earlier wooden tower from 1909
facts.status_note: Standing as a display at the Patten Lumbermen's Museum; the original Chase Mountain site is listed as gone

access.note: On display at a museum that charges admission; the sources do not say whether the tower can be climbed

events.note: Wooden tower established on the summit; a one-room watchman's cabin was built the same year
Replaced by a steel tower; the 1917 annual report gives 16 feet
Watchman's one-room cabin replaced by a second, larger cabin
Taken down on Mount Chase and moved to the Patten Lumbermen's Museum

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts 1917 entry and the two hiking pages give 16 feet. Forest Lookouts' 1920 inventory gives 12 feet. The story reports both and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Relocation year 2001 is supported by FFLOS, the 1HappyHiker blog and Maine IAT, which may share an FFLA source. Suggest adding a 2001 year to the Patten record's relocated event, which has none. Staffing: no names or dates beyond the 1909-1922 watchman cabin. Access: no source says whether the tower can be climbed; the museum page gives only general visiting details. Photos: a Patten Lumbermen's Museum Facebook post about the tower's removal exists (search snippet only, not read, license unknown), so no photo entry was added. Design height left as a conflict, not a fact.
